crime: One prisoner kept the fire going in the lounge fireplace and warmed every girl's hands in turn. Each dusk, {WITCH_NAME} walked out with her to gather kindling.
One dusk in the forest, the girl rubbed {WITCH_NAME}'s hands warm, then let go to lift the kindling. Asked to stay by her side all evening, she said only, "For a while. The others are cold too."
{WITCH_NAME}'s father used to come home a few nights a season and warm her hands at the stove. "Back before it goes cold," he would say, and she would wake to a cold stove and his boots gone.

There among the trees, {WITCH_NAME} looped the kindling cord around the girl's throat from behind and pulled until the girl went still. Then she called the girl's likeness out of the air beside her: a warm hand in hers that did not let go.

Back in the lounge, in plain sight of everyone, the likeness built up the fire in the fireplace and sat at {WITCH_NAME}'s side the whole evening. At dinner in the dining hall, as the first snow began to fall outside, it rubbed a shivering prisoner's hands warm. Just before lockup, {WITCH_NAME} walked it out through the entrance hall for the last of the wood, came straight back alone, and stayed by the fire until the doors were locked.

The next morning, the prisoners found the girl in the forest under the night's snow, strangled with the kindling cord. In the trial court, they took it that she had been killed after going out for wood, while {WITCH_NAME} sat among them by the fire.

Then the prisoner who had lifted her from the snow spoke up. The ground beneath her had been bare, without a single flake. She had been lying there before the first snow fell, so the girl who warmed hands at dinner had been {WITCH_NAME}'s likeness.
fields.epitaph: The only warmth that never let go of her was the one she remembered into being.
fields.epithet: The girl whose hands were only ever warmed by someone on the way out
execution: The execution stand raised a narrow iron bench with an iron figure at each end and chained her, seated, at its middle. The two figures sat down and slid in along the bench toward her from either side, their cold iron shoulders pressing closer and closer. They folded their iron hands over hers and did not let go. She stopped stirring between them, and still the iron company stayed at her sides.

magic.name: Remembered Company
magic.text: She calls anyone she has ever known to her side, warm, solid, and just as she remembers them.
